stem: A hospitalized client with a confirmed complicated urinary tract infection is receiving empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics. Urine culture identification and susceptibility results are now available. Which change in the treatment plan is most consistent with current guidance?

options.A: Continue the same broad-spectrum regimen for the entire course regardless of susceptibility results
options.B: Select an effective antibiotic with a targeted spectrum based on the urine culture identification and susceptibility results
options.C: Stop antimicrobial therapy because a positive culture alone indicates asymptomatic bacteriuria
options.D: Repeat urine cultures daily and delay any treatment adjustment until cultures become negative

rationale: The 2025 IDSA complicated UTI guideline recommends that, once urine culture identification and susceptibility results are available in a microbiologically confirmed complicated UTI, definitive therapy should use an effective antibiotic with a targeted spectrum rather than continuing empiric broad-spectrum therapy for the full course. Therefore B is correct. A ignores the recommendation to narrow definitive therapy when microbiologic data are available. C is incorrect because the client has a confirmed symptomatic complicated UTI, not asymptomatic bacteriuria. D is not recommended; CDC urine-culture stewardship guidance states that cultures should not routinely be obtained simply to document response when symptoms are resolving.
educational_objective: Use urine culture identification and susceptibility data to recognize when empiric broad-spectrum UTI therapy should transition to targeted definitive antimicrobial therapy.
source_organization: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA); Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: IDSA 2025 Guideline Update on Complicated Urinary Tract Infections; Urine Culture Stewardship in Patients without Indwelling Urinary Catheters
source_version_date: IDSA published 2025-07-17, section reviewed 2025-05-12; CDC current guidance accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: IDSA 2025 cUTI Guideline > Recommendations on Selection of Antibiotic Therapy > C. Selection of Definitive Antibiotic Therapy: in microbiologically confirmed cUTI, select a definitive effective antibiotic with a targeted spectrum based on urine culture identification and susceptibility as soon as available rather than continuing empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics for the complete duration. CDC Urine Culture Stewardship > Inappropriate uses: urine culture to document response to therapy unless symptoms fail to resolve.
source_claim_supported: For confirmed complicated UTI, available culture identification and susceptibility results should guide targeted definitive antimicrobial therapy rather than automatic continuation of broad empiric coverage.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed page 12, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: Review pertinent data prior to medication administration (e.g., contraindications, lab results, allergies, potential interactions) and evaluate client response to medication.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — antimicrobial therapy adjustment using culture/susceptibility data
correction_summary: Removed the unsupported notion of one universal urine-culture colony threshold and rebuilt the item around a current IDSA 2025 culture-directed antimicrobial decision. Corrected the blueprint from Reduction of Risk Potential to Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies.
audit_findings: IDSA 2025 directly supports narrowing confirmed cUTI therapy to an effective targeted agent using culture identification/susceptibility results. CDC independently supports avoiding routine repeat cultures solely to document response. B uniquely matches guidance; A contradicts de-escalation guidance; C misclassifies symptomatic infection as ASB; D conflicts with culture stewardship. No unsupported dose, colony count, duration, resistance threshold, second answer, cueing, or unresolved conflict remains. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
